items.markingKey: Context (Chinese property developer Evergrande accumulated liabilities of over $300 bn and was ordered to liquidate by a Hong Kong court in January 2024.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Very high borrowing to fund growth left it unable to service its debts when property sales fell – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to gearing and financial risk.

items.stem: Mekong Furniture has cash of $8,000, trade receivables of $20,000, inventories of $80,000, trade payables of $50,000 and a bank overdraft of $15,000, all due within 30 days. Calculate the current ratio and the acid-test ratio, and comment on the risk that the business becomes insolvent.
items.answer: Current ratio = 108,000/65,000 = 1.66:1; acid-test = 28,000/65,000 = 0.43:1. Liquid assets do not cover current liabilities, so it may be unable to pay its debts as they fall due unless it sells stock quickly – a real risk of insolvency.
items.markingKey: current assets 108,000; current liabilities 65,000; ratios 1.66 and 0.43. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both ratios. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [1] comment on insolvency risk.

items.stem:
Strong demand for AI chips pushed Nvidia's gross margin to over 70% in its 2024-25 financial year.

Using the information and your knowledge of business management, evaluate whether ROCE is the most important ratio for judging the performance of a business, and recommend what the organization should do. [10]
items.answer: ROCE is a key summary of performance, but it should be used with liquidity, efficiency and non-financial measures.
items.markingKey: Supporting: combines profit and capital used; comparable with interest rates; used by investors. Challenging: ignores liquidity and cash flow; can be distorted by old, depreciated assets; short-term focus; industry differences. Recommendation: ROCE is a key summary of performance, but it should be used with liquidity, efficiency and non-financial measures. items.stem:
Large supermarkets such as Tesco usually report current ratios below 1 because they sell inventory quickly for cash while paying suppliers weeks later.

Using the extract where relevant, analyse the advantages and disadvantages of acting on the view that liquidity ratios give a reliable picture of a business's financial health. [8]
items.answer: They are useful warning signs but should be read alongside cash-flow forecasts, industry norms and trends.
items.markingKey: Advantages: quick indicators of ability to pay debts; comparable over time; warn of insolvency risk. Disadvantages: snapshot at one date (window dressing); industry norms differ; ignore timing of cash flows; need cash-flow forecasts too. 7-8: balanced analysis applied to the case; 5-6: analysis of both sides, partly applied; 3-4: one-sided or generic; 1-2: descriptive.

Using the extract where relevant, analyse the advantages and disadvantages of acting on the view that efficiency ratios are more useful than profitability ratios for managers. [8]
items.answer: Efficiency ratios help managers control operations, but they must be used alongside profitability and liquidity ratios.
items.markingKey: Advantages: show how well working capital is managed; identify causes of cash problems; operational targets. Disadvantages: profitability determines survival and returns; efficiency norms vary by industry; both needed for full picture. 7-8: balanced analysis applied to the case; 5-6: analysis of both sides, partly applied; 3-4: one-sided or generic; 1-2: descriptive.

items.stem:
UK discount retailer Wilko entered administration in August 2023; about 12,500 jobs were lost and stores closed after no buyer was found for the whole business.

"Ratio analysis is of limited value in predicting business failure." With reference to Wilko's administration, discuss this statement. [10]
items.answer: Ratios give useful warnings, especially in trends, but predicting failure also requires cash-flow forecasts and qualitative judgement.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: historical data; window dressing; qualitative factors omitted; failure often sudden. Arguments against: trends in liquidity and gearing give early warnings; used by lenders and investors; combined ratios (e.g. Altman Z-score) predict failure. Judgement: Ratios give useful warnings, especially in trends, but predicting failure also requires cash-flow forecasts and qualitative judgement. items.stem: ROCE measures:
options: how efficiently a business uses its long-term capital to generate profit
the ability to pay short-term debts
items.answer: how efficiently a business uses its long-term capital to generate profit
items.markingKey: C. Profit relative to capital employed.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The ability of a business to pay its short-term debts as they fall due"?
items.answer: liquidity
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of liquidity.

items.answer: A business with a gearing ratio above 50%, financed mainly by long-term debt

items.stem: Briefly explain why ratio analysis should be used with caution when comparing two businesses.
items.answer: They may use different accounting policies (depreciation, stock valuation), have different year-ends and operate in different markets, so ratios are not directly comparable.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: They may use different accounting policies (depreciation, stock valuation), have different year-ends and operate in different markets, so ratios are not directly comparable. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

Explain why profitability ratios should be compared with other businesses in the same industry. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: Margins vary greatly by industry (supermarkets have low margins, software firms high), so only comparisons with similar firms or over time show whether performance is good.
items.markingKey: Margins vary greatly by industry (supermarkets have low margins, software firms high), so only comparisons with similar firms or over time show whether performance is good. items.stem: A student claims: "A business that is insolvent must immediately close down." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It may enter administration, restructure debts, be sold or be rescued; liquidation is only one possible outcome.
items.markingKey: It may enter administration, restructure debts, be sold or be rescued; liquidation is only one possible outcome. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between the profit margin and the gross profit margin.
items.answer: The GPM shows profit after cost of sales as a share of revenue (pricing and production costs); the profit margin also deducts expenses, showing overall cost control.
items.markingKey: The GPM shows profit after cost of sales as a share of revenue (pricing and production costs); the profit margin also deducts expenses, showing overall cost control. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With reference to the collapse of Thomas Cook, explain how it illustrates liquidity.
items.answer: Travel company Thomas Cook collapsed in September 2019 after failing to raise £200 m of extra funds, stranding about 150,000 UK customers abroad. Large debts and insufficient cash meant it could not meet short-term obligations
items.markingKey: Context (Travel company Thomas Cook collapsed in September 2019 after failing to raise £200 m of extra funds, stranding about 150,000 UK customers abroad.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Large debts and insufficient cash meant it could not meet short-term obligations – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to liquidity.

items.markingKey: Context (Inditex (Zara) designs and delivers new styles to stores within weeks and holds less inventory than many rivals, with stock turning over faster.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.answer: UK discount retailer Wilko entered administration in August 2023; about 12,500 jobs were lost and stores closed after no buyer was found for the whole business. Administration attempted a rescue before the business was broken up and liquidated
items.markingKey: Context (UK discount retailer Wilko entered administration in August 2023; about 12,500 jobs were lost and stores closed after no buyer was found for the whole business.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Tasman Surf Co. reports revenue of $200,000, gross profit of $80,000 and PBIT of $32,000. Non-current liabilities plus equity total $900,000. Calculate the profit margin and the return on capital employed (ROCE).
items.answer: Profit margin = 16.0%; ROCE = 3.6%
items.markingKey: PM = PBIT/revenue × 100 = 16.0%; ROCE = PBIT/capital employed × 100 = 32,000/900,000 × 100 = 3.6%. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both ratios. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.answer: Industries such as supermarkets and fast food operate safely below 1 because they sell for cash and receive credit from suppliers; context and trends matter.
items.markingKey: Industries such as supermarkets and fast food operate safely below 1 because they sell for cash and receive credit from suppliers; context and trends matter. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.
